title: Applied anatomy: neck triangles, the parotid gland and the facial nerve

related.why: Thoracic inlet: the root of the neck below these triangles

brief.scenario: A 58-year-old woman has a firm 3 cm swelling in the left parotid region and weakness of the left side of her face. This is a verbal viva: the examiner will ask about the neck and the parotid region, and will read out a description of an operative view of the gland.
brief.task: Answer the examiner's questions on the triangles of the neck, the parotid gland and the facial nerve, including the written description the examiner reads out, and relate them to her findings.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Where the gland sits, what runs through it, and what her facial weakness means.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Forgetting that a lesion of the nerve trunk in the parotid weakens the whole half of the face, forehead included.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "A parotid mass with facial weakness is malignant until proven otherwise."

grid.label: Neck triangles
grid.fail: Cannot give the borders of either triangle.
grid.pass: Anterior: midline, lower border of mandible, sternocleidomastoid. Posterior: sternocleidomastoid, trapezius, middle third of clavicle.
grid.high: Subdivides the anterior triangle (submental, submandibular, carotid, muscular); names the accessory nerve crossing the posterior triangle.

grid.label: Parotid relations
grid.fail: Cannot say where the gland lies or where the duct opens.
grid.pass: Over masseter and the ramus, from zygomatic arch to below the angle, back to mastoid; duct opens opposite the upper second molar.
grid.high: Deep lobe reaches the parapharyngeal space, so a deep lobe tumour can push the tonsil and soft palate medially.

grid.label: Structures in the gland
grid.fail: Does not know the facial nerve runs through the gland.
grid.pass: Superficial to deep: facial nerve, retromandibular vein, external carotid artery. The nerve plane separates superficial and deep lobes.
grid.high: Nerve leaves the stylomastoid foramen; at surgery the tragal pointer and posterior belly of digastric lead to the trunk.

grid.label: Testing the branches
grid.fail: Tests only a smile or an eyebrow raise.
grid.pass: Temporal: raise eyebrows. Zygomatic: close eyes tightly. Buccal: puff cheeks, show teeth. Marginal mandibular: lower lip. Cervical: platysma.
grid.high: Grades overall function with House-Brackmann; temporal and marginal mandibular branches have few cross-connections, so their weakness shows most.

grid.label: Upper or lower motor neurone
grid.fail: Says forehead sparing with an otherwise complete half-face palsy is typical of a parotid tumour.
grid.pass: Whole half of face weak, forehead included: lower motor neurone, fits the parotid. Forehead sparing with a complete lower-face palsy suggests upper motor neurone.
grid.high: Explains the bilateral cortical input to the upper face, and that a parotid tumour can weaken single branches and spare the forehead.

grid.label: Meaning and next steps
grid.fail: Calls it a pleomorphic adenoma and offers routine follow-up.
grid.pass: Treats it as malignant until proven otherwise: ultrasound with guided fine-needle aspiration or core biopsy, and MRI.
grid.high: Examines the scalp and face for a skin cancer draining to parotid nodes, and the neck nodes; refers to the head and neck MDT.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: What are the borders of the posterior triangle?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: The trapezius and the mandible, I think.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Where does the parotid duct open?

fail.text: What runs through the parotid gland?

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: How would you test her facial nerve?

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Her forehead moves normally on both sides. Does that fit?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Yes, that's typical of a parotid tumour.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: A pleomorphic adenoma. I'd see her in clinic.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: What are the borders of the neck triangles?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: The anterior triangle is the midline, the lower border of the mandible and sternocleidomastoid. The posterior triangle is sternocleidomastoid, trapezius and the middle third of the clavicle.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Over masseter and the ramus, from the zygomatic arch to below the angle of the mandible, back to the mastoid. The duct opens opposite the upper second molar.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: From superficial to deep, the facial nerve, the retromandibular vein and the external carotid artery. The nerve plane separates the superficial and deep lobes.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Test the facial nerve for me.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Raise your eyebrows for temporal, close your eyes tightly for zygomatic, puff your cheeks and show your teeth for buccal, pull your lower lip down for marginal mandibular, and tense the neck for cervical.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: The whole left side is weak, including the forehead. What does that tell you?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: It's a lower motor neurone lesion, which fits the parotid. If the forehead were spared I'd think of an upper motor neurone lesion instead.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: A parotid mass with facial weakness is malignant until proven otherwise. Ultrasound with guided FNA or core biopsy, and an MRI.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: The anterior triangle subdivides into submental, submandibular, carotid and muscular triangles. The accessory nerve crosses the posterior triangle, where it's at risk in node biopsy.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Could a tumour here present inside the mouth?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Yes. The deep lobe reaches the parapharyngeal space, so a deep lobe tumour can push the tonsil and soft palate medially.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: How would a surgeon find the nerve?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: It leaves the stylomastoid foramen. The tragal pointer and the posterior belly of digastric lead to the trunk before it divides.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I'd grade overall function with House-Brackmann. The temporal and marginal mandibular branches have few cross-connections, so weakness shows most there.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Why is the forehead spared in a stroke?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: The part of the facial nucleus supplying the upper face gets input from both hemispheres. But a parotid tumour can also involve only some branches, so a spared forehead doesn't rule the parotid out. That's why I test each branch.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I'd look at her scalp and face for a skin cancer draining to the parotid nodes, and examine the neck nodes. Then refer to the head and neck MDT.

failures.move: Calling forehead sparing with a complete lower-face palsy typical of a parotid tumour.
failures.consequence: Misses a possible upper motor neurone cause such as a stroke.

failures.move: Calling a mass with facial weakness benign.
failures.consequence: Delays diagnosis of a likely malignancy.
Misses partial weakness in a single branch.

recovery.line: Whole half of the face including the forehead is lower motor neurone; forehead sparing with a complete lower-face palsy suggests upper motor neurone.
Nerve, vein, artery, from superficial to deep.

knowledge.fact: Parotid contents, superficial to deep: facial nerve, retromandibular vein, external carotid artery.
Duct crosses masseter, pierces buccinator, opens opposite the upper second molar.
Five branches: temporal, zygomatic, buccal, marginal mandibular, cervical.
Trunk lesion (lower motor neurone): whole half of face weak. Forehead sparing with complete lower-face palsy: upper motor neurone. Parotid tumours can also cause branch palsies.
Parotid mass with facial weakness: treat as malignant; ultrasound-guided sampling and MRI.

recall.think: Facial weakness with a parotid mass means malignancy until proven otherwise.
recall.say: "Lower motor neurone: the forehead is weak too."
do: Look for skin primary and neck nodes

numbers.meaning: temporal, zygomatic, buccal, marginal mandibular, cervical

recall.trap: Forehead sparing with a complete lower-face palsy suggests an upper motor neurone cause; test every branch.
recall.finish: Ultrasound-guided biopsy, MRI, head and neck MDT.

partner.opening: This is a verbal viva on the neck and parotid. Tell me the borders of the triangles of the neck.

reveals.finding: Firm, fixed, non-tender 3 cm mass in the left parotid region. Duct opening normal.

reveals.trigger: Candidate has described where the parotid lies
reveals.finding: Read out: in an operative view of the left parotid after the superficial part of the gland has been lifted, a single nerve trunk divides within the gland into five branches. They run upwards to the forehead, forwards across the cheekbone, forwards across the cheek, along the lower border of the mandible, and down into the neck. Deep to the nerve, a large vein runs vertically behind the ramus of the mandible. Ask: name the branches, and what lies in the gland deep to this vein?

reveals.trigger: Candidate describes testing the facial nerve
reveals.finding: Weakness of the whole left side of the face, including the forehead. Eye closure incomplete.
A firm 1.5 cm node in the left upper neck.

push.question: What are the borders of the triangles?
push.expect: Anterior: midline, mandible, SCM. Posterior: SCM, trapezius, clavicle.

push.question: What passes through the parotid?
push.expect: Facial nerve, retromandibular vein, external carotid artery, superficial to deep.

push.question: Upper or lower motor neurone?
push.expect: Lower: forehead involved. Forehead sparing with a complete lower-face palsy would suggest upper; partial branch palsies can spare it.

push.question: What would you do next?
push.expect: Ultrasound-guided FNA or core biopsy, MRI, look for skin primary, head and neck MDT.

curveballs.prompt: She has an ulcerated lesion on her left temple.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Possible cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma with metastasis to the parotid nodes. Biopsy both.

curveballs.prompt: After parotidectomy she sweats over the cheek when she eats. Why?
curveballs.safeAnswer: Frey's syndrome: cut parasympathetic fibres to the parotid regrow into the sweat glands of the skin.

curveballs.prompt: How might a deep lobe tumour present?
curveballs.safeAnswer: As a mass pushing the tonsil and soft palate medially, from the parapharyngeal space.
